sty_ad6b92691f1f6bd0.summary: A recent study introduces a hybrid approach to semantic search that balances privacy and efficiency. The method employs a public singular value decomposition (SVD) basis and product quantization (PQ) index for client-side candidate selection, with candidate identifiers disclosed. Queries are encrypted using the CKKS scheme during reranking, enabling secure scoring of provider vectors. Performance improvements include significant reductions in server processing time and response size. Evaluation on a subset of BEIR queries shows comparable effectiveness between encrypted and plaintext reranking in most collections. However, the approach does not fully protect against semantic-query, document, unlinkability, circuit, or access-pattern privacy, as some information leakage remains through disclosed candidate sets and public PQ data.

sty_10c633ae2c2d5d92.summary: Researchers have proposed two new sparsity regularizers for Top-k sparse autoencoders (SAEs), a tool used to interpret vision foundation models by decomposing their activations into sparse, monosemantic features. Traditionally, Top-k SAEs enforce sparsity by retaining only the k most active latent units per input, avoiding explicit sparsity penalties like the \(\ell_1\) norm. However, the study introduces an \(\ell_1\) penalty on unselected units and a scale-invariant \(\ell_1/\ell_2\) ratio penalty applied before the Top-k selection. These regularizers improve the selectivity and interpretability of the latent codes without compromising reconstruction quality. The \(\ell_1/\ell_2\) penalty also enhances robustness to the choice of k during inference and benefits small-budget linear probing. The findings suggest that combining architectural sparsity with soft sparsity regularization can yield complementary advantages.

output_cleanup.title: Researchers introduce JoLT, a near-lossless KV cache compression method using joint Tucker decomposition and JL-residual allocation for large language models achieving 2-3x compression with minimal accuracy loss
output_cleanup.description:
Researchers present JoLT, a new method for compressing the key-value (KV) cache in transformer models, which is a major memory bottleneck during inference. JoLT applies a partial Tucker decomposition to compress token and feature axes while preserving head and layer axes, combined with a Johnson-Lindenstrauss rotated low-bit residual to recover discarded information, achieving near-lossless 2-3x compression without degrading model performance on benchmarks like GSM8K and RULER across models including Mistral-7B-v0.3 and LLaMA-2-13B.

JoLT uses a Lagrangian dual to allocate compression parameters under a one-byte budget per layer group, separately for keys and values. It achieves reconstruction errors significantly lower than prior methods like cross-layer SVD and 4-bit quantization. A variant called FlashJoLT employs randomized SVD to speed up compression by 5-13 times while maintaining quality. This approach addresses the KV cache's growth with batch size, context length, and depth, which limits throughput more than model weights at long contexts.

output_cleanup.title: Researchers formalize matched comparison methods to rigorously assess extractable memorization in large language models, addressing validity issues in prior studies
output_cleanup.description:
Recent research identifies validity problems in claims of extractable memorization in large language models (LLMs), where some studies overstate memorization by using sequences too short to distinguish it from predictability, while others question extraction as evidence of memorization. The authors propose a rigorous approach requiring matched comparisons of generation probabilities between training and non-training sequences to establish a valid memorization claim. They formalize this through a conformal test for population samples and a census method for single documents, enabling calibrated thresholds for memorization detection.

Applying these methods to models like OLMo 2 32B on Wikipedia and Llama 3.1 70B on books, the study reveals that some previously reported memorization rates reflect false positives rather than true memorization. The calibrated thresholds can be extremely low, supporting memorization claims only when sequences are generated with near certainty within realistic sampling budgets. Based on these findings, the authors refine the definition of extractable memorization to require both a valid memorization claim and near-certain generation feasibility.

output_cleanup.description: Researchers investigated whether language models can continually learn and retain new facts in their weights after training by testing invented facts written into Qwen3 models through sequences of up to one hundred later writes. They found that training with diverse restatements significantly improves the model's ability to use facts compared to bare-statement training, with broad data retaining 46% accuracy after twenty writes versus 1% for bare statements. However, facts can be behaviorally forgotten without being erased, and later writes redirect which questions reach stored knowledge, causing interference regardless of storage method. The study concludes that while broad data and frozen references help preserve capability, no tested intervention maintains earlier facts in weights reliably, suggesting context remains the more dependable channel for composing and preserving facts over time.
